attachment.snippet:
1	# Market
2	
3	The competitive landscape for Claudinite: the open substrate standards every
4	coding-agent user already has on disk, and the direct competitors solving the
5	same problem Claudinite does — keeping AI-coding-agent conventions consistent
6	and current across many repositories.
7	
8	## Key insights
9	
10	- The substrate formats don't propagate a convention across repos — that gap, not the files themselves, is what Claudinite sells against.
11	- AGENTS.md is the standard to read, not displace: 30+ agents, 60,000+ repos, now under the Linux Foundation.
12	- A small competitor category sits on the same gap: knowhub, ai-rules-sync, ai-rules, Sync AI Agent Rules.
13	- Those competitors move files; Claudinite moves checks, skills and tasks as one vendored unit — the sharpest gap available.
14	
15	## The substrate: per-repo convention files
16	
17	Every agent-facing repo already carries at least one plain-text convention
18	file, and Claudinite has to interoperate with all of them rather than compete
19	with them:
20	
21	- **AGENTS.md** is the vendor-neutral standard: a plain-markdown, no-frontmatter
22	  file at the repo root, formalized as an open spec in August 2025 with OpenAI,
23	  Google, Cursor, and Factory participating, then donated to the Linux
24	  Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation in December 2025. By December 2025 it was
25	  read by 30+ agents (Codex, Claude Code via import, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini
26	  CLI, Jules, Factory, Aider, Zed, VS Code, Windsurf, Devin) across 60,000+
27	  repos.
28	- **CLAUDE.md** is Claude Code's own project-memory file, pulled into every
29	  session automatically. Community best-practice converges on keeping it under
30	  ~200 lines, universally-applicable only, and using file-path references
31	  instead of pasting detail inline — the same "progressive disclosure" shape
32	  Claudinite's pack system (always-loaded `RULES.md` plus skills/checks pulled
33	  in on demand) formalizes structurally instead of leaving to author
34	  discipline.
35	- **Cursor** has moved from a single `.cursorrules` file to a `.cursor/rules/`
36	  directory, with per-file and combined character caps (6,000 / 12,000) and
37	  mention-triggered activation.
38	- **Windsurf** carries `global_rules.md` plus `.windsurf/rules/` (discovered
39	  walking up to the git root), with the legacy `.windsurfrules` still
40	  supported.
41	- **GitHub Copilot** uses `.github/copilot-instructions.md`; unlike Cursor and
42	  Windsurf it has no mention-triggered rule activation.
43	
44	None of these substrate formats natively answer the question Claudinite is
45	for: how the *same* convention, once refined, reaches every repo that shares
46	it, and stays current there without hand-copying.
47	
48	## Direct competitors: syncing rules across repos
49	
50	A distinct, smaller tool category has formed around exactly that gap —
51	propagating shared agent rules across many repositories:
52	
53	- **knowhub** — teams edit rules in one shared source and rerun a sync in each
54	  repo to pull in diffed updates, so no repo falls behind.
55	- **ai-rules-sync (lbb00)** — syncs/manages agent rules, skills, commands, and
56	  subagents across many agent tools at once (Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot,
57	  OpenCode, Trae AI, Codex, Gemini CLI, Warp).
58	- **ai-rules (fabian-barney)** — a shared rules/guidance repo consumed by
59	  multiple projects.
60	- **Sync AI Agent Rules** (GitHub Action) — a marketplace action wrapping the
61	  same sync-on-CI idea.
62	- **Antigravity Lab's multi-repo governance notes** frame the underlying
63	  design problem directly: keeping agent behavior consistent across separate
64	  repos via sync scripts and drift detection.
65	
66	Where these tools mostly move **files** (copy/symlink the latest rule text
67	into place), Claudinite's pack model additionally carries **enforcement**
68	(checks that fail a session or CI on drift), **procedure** (skills), and
69	**scheduled work** (tasks) as one versioned, vendored unit per pack — the
70	differentiation to sharpen with more research below.
71	
72	## Sources
73	
74	- [AGENTS.md Complete Guide 2026: Spec, Tools, Examples](https://codersera.com/blog/agents-md-complete-guide-2026/)
75	- [Top AI Agent Standards to Know in 2026 — Agentailor](https://blog.agentailor.com/posts/top-ai-agent-standards-2026)
76	- [CLAUDE.md Best Practices: The Complete 2026 Guide — DEV Community](https://dev.to/nishilbhave/claudemd-best-practices-the-complete-2026-guide-435j)
77	- [Best practices for Claude Code — Claude Code Docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)
78	- [Cursor vs Windsurf vs GitHub Copilot in 2026 — CodeAnt](https://www.codeant.ai/blogs/best-ai-code-editor-cursor-vs-windsurf-vs-copilot)
79	- [Cursor Rules vs CLAUDE.md vs Copilot Instructions — Agent Rules Builder](https://www.agentrulegen.com/guides/cursorrules-vs-claude-md)
80	- [ai-rules-sync — GitHub](https://github.com/lbb00/ai-rules-sync)
81	- [fabian-barney/ai-rules — GitHub](https://github.com/fabian-barney/ai-rules)
82	- [Introducing knowhub: Share AI Assistant Rules Across Repos — Medium](https://medium.com/@yujiisobe/introducing-knowhub-share-ai-assistant-rules-across-repos-17fb6b09c114)
83	- [Sync AI Agent Rules — GitHub Marketplace](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/sync-ai-agent-rules)
84	- [Keeping Agent Behavior Consistent Across Separate Repositories: Notes on Multi-Repo Governance — Antigravity Lab](https://antigravitylab.net/en/articles/antigravity/antigravity-multi-repo-agent-governance-design)
85	
86	## Open questions
87	
88	- Do any of knowhub, ai-rules-sync, or ai-rules ship enforcement (a failing
89	  check/CI gate), or are they purely file-propagation — the exact axis
90	  Claudinite's pack model (checks + skills + tasks, not just prose) would
91	  differentiate on?
92	- What are the adoption numbers (repos, orgs, GitHub stars) for knowhub and
93	  ai-rules-sync, to size this category against AGENTS.md's 60,000+ repos?
94	- Is there a pricing/business model for any of these — are they OSS-only, or
95	  does anyone charge for a hosted sync/registry service (relevant to
96	  Claudinite's own commercial positioning)?
97	- Does the AGENTS.md spec (via the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation)
98	  say anything about layering enforcement or packaged conventions on top of
99	  the base file, or is that explicitly out of its scope?
100	- How do knowhub and ai-rules-sync *market* themselves (headline claim, named
101	  audience, adoption CTA)? claudinite.com launched on the
102	  enforcement/procedure/scheduled-work differentiation (see
103	  [Website wiki](../Website/README.md)) — worth checking whether any
104	  competitor has started claiming enforcement too, which would blunt that
105	  message.
106	
107	## Growth log
108	
109	- **2026-07-28** — initial seed: substrate standards (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md,
110	  Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot) and the direct rule-sync competitor set
111	  (knowhub, ai-rules-sync, ai-rules) researched and cited.
112	- **2026-07-28** — open question added by the website build: how competitors
113	  market themselves, to defend the enforcement-differentiation message the
114	  launched site leads with.

1	# Website
2	
3	The marketing site itself as a research subject: the positioning, promoted
4	features, and conversion decisions behind claudinite.com (`site/` in this
5	repo), recorded so future passes can revisit them against evidence instead of
6	re-deriving them. The site is built for frequent agentic refreshes — the
7	rotating promo content lives in one data file
8	([site/data/promoted.js](../../site/data/promoted.js), contract in
9	[site/README.md](../../site/README.md)); this page is where the *reasoning*
10	behind what gets promoted accumulates.
11	
12	## Key insights
13	
14	- The headline names the substrate pain, not the category — "convention packs" means nothing to a cold visitor.
15	- Promoted differentiation is the Market wiki's sharpest gap: rivals move files, Claudinite moves enforcement and procedure.
16	- A scheduled promo pass edits one data file and cannot break layout; mechanism explanations stay static HTML.
17	- No invented testimonials, stars or adoption numbers until real proof points exist — hence zero social proof today.
18	
19	## Positioning decisions (2026-07-28, initial)
20	
21	Decisions made for launch — owner-editable calls, not researched claims; the
22	research they lean on is the [Market wiki](../Market/README.md):
23	
24	- **Audience**: teams running Claude Code / AI coding agents across many
25	  repositories; the individual staff-plus engineer as the entry point.
26	- **Headline**: "Stop copy-pasting agent rules." Names the substrate pain
27	  (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md copies drifting) rather than the category, because the
28	  category ("convention packs") is unknown to cold visitors.
29	- **Differentiation promoted above the fold-adjacent sections**: competitors
30	  move *files*; Claudinite moves *enforcement (checks), procedure (skills),
31	  and scheduled work (tasks)* as one versioned unit — the axis the Market
32	  wiki identifies as the sharpest available gap.
33	- **Promoted features (initial four, ordered)**: enforced checks; nightly
34	  baselining; the growth loop; scheduled upkeep. Chosen because each is a
35	  mechanism competitors in the rule-sync category demonstrably lack, and each
36	  has a visual explanation on the page (animated: fleet sync, session loop,
37	  baselining board, growth loop).
38	- **Primary conversion action**: adopt Claudinite in a repo (the "one
39	  conversation to adopt" section); secondary: visit the canon repository.
40	  Trust reducers placed at the decision point: no server/account, vendored
41	  plain files, every automated change is a PR through CI, leave by deleting a
42	  directory.
43	- **Style**: monochrome ink-on-paper with one malachite accent, large
44	  grotesk headlines, terminal demos, generous whitespace — modeled on
45	  paperclip.ing's typography-led minimalism (see Sources) but with an
46	  ownable mineral/crystal motif; check-state semantics (red blocking, amber
47	  advisory, green pass) are the only other colors.
48	- **Honesty constraint**: no invented testimonials, stars, or adoption
49	  numbers anywhere on the site; social proof waits until real proof points
50	  exist (see Open questions).
51	
52	## Site architecture for agentic updates
53	
54	- Evergreen mechanism explanations are static HTML (`site/index.html`);
55	  rotating promo content (stats, spotlight, pack cards, dated updates) is
56	  data-driven from `site/data/promoted.js` and rendered client-side, so a
57	  scheduled promo pass edits one file and cannot break layout.
58	- Deploys ride GitHub Pages' artifact flow
59	  ([deploy-pages.yml](../../.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml)) on pushes to
60	  `main` touching `site/**`; the claudinite.com domain is attached in the
61	  repository's Pages settings.
62	
63	## Sources
64	
65	- [Paperclip](https://paperclip.ing/) — the style reference: monochrome,
66	  typography-led SaaS landing page; hero → features → proof → one-command
67	  install CTA structure, FAQ for objection handling.
68	
69	The competitive claims the positioning leans on are cited in the
70	[Market wiki](../Market/README.md), not re-cited here; decisions recorded on
71	this page are owner calls, not researched claims.
72	
73	## Open questions
74	
75	- **Social proof**: what real proof points exist to put on the site — count
76	  of repos on the home fleet, canon commit cadence, GitHub stars once the
77	  canon repo is public? The site currently ships zero testimonials/numbers
78	  by design.
79	- **Canon repo visibility**: the site's CTAs link
80	  `github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite` — is that repo public? If not, what
81	  should "Get Claudinite" point to until it is?
82	- **Domain + analytics**: is claudinite.com DNS connected to Pages yet, and
83	  do we want privacy-respecting analytics (e.g. no-cookie counters) to learn
84	  which promoted features draw clicks on the adopt CTA?
85	- **Commercial model**: the site presents Claudinite as adoptable OSS-style
86	  tooling with no pricing page — `product-requirements/` is still empty;
87	  when a business model is distilled there, the site needs a pricing/plans
88	  decision (relates to the Market wiki's open question on competitor
89	  pricing).
90	- **Messaging test**: does "Stop copy-pasting agent rules" outperform a
91	  category-first headline ("Convention packs for AI coding agents") with the
92	  target audience? Worth a lightweight test once traffic exists.
93	- **OG/social image**: the page has no raster og:image yet (SVG-only
94	  assets); generate one so link shares render a card.
95	
96	## Growth log
97	
98	- **2026-07-28** — page created alongside the initial site build: launch
99	  positioning, promoted-feature choices, agentic-update architecture, and
100	  the conversion strategy recorded; open questions seeded for future passes.

input.head: claude/per-repo-baselining-d9v18j
input.title: baselining: fail the run when the maintenance PR cannot be opened
input.body:
## The defect

`deliver()` in `packs/basics/tasks/baselining/worker.mjs` destructured only `json` from the PR-open POST and never read `status`:

```js
({ json: pr } = await gh(token, `/repos/${repo}/pulls`, { method: 'POST', ... }));
```

When that POST fails, the error body lands in `pr`. `pr.node_id` is undefined so the auto-merge arm is skipped silently, the CI dispatch has no PR to attach to, and the run still reports `ok`.

## Why it compounds

`openMaintenancePull` reuses by **open PR**, not by branch. A cycle that pushes its branch but fails to open the PR therefore finds nothing to reuse next cycle and mints a *fresh* branch — nightly — while the stamp never advances and nothing surfaces the failure.

## What it did to the fleet

Observed 2026-07-29/30 across all twelve consumers. Every repo except the GCEC pilot sat on canon ref `7e89c0cf` (2026-07-28) carrying `claudinite/maintenance-2026-07-29-*` and `-07-30-*` branches with **no PR behind either**, and several carried two branches for a single day. GCEC — where the Actions PR permission is enabled — opened and merged its maintenance PRs normally throughout.

The usual cause is repo-level and invisible from inside the Action: *Settings → Actions → General → "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests"* is off, so the POST 403s. The thrown message names that remedy rather than leaving a bare status code.

## The change

- `pullCreateError(status, json)` — a pure predicate, `null` only on a 201 carrying a PR number, else the message to fail on
- `deliver()` throws on it instead of continuing with an error body

Extracted as a pure helper to match the file's existing test surface (`normalizeDelivery`, `ciDispatchPlan`, …), with see-it-fail coverage for the 403, a 201 with no PR number, and the no-message fallback.

## Verification

Full CI test set **1015 pass / 0 fail**; `check_the_world` **0 blocking, 9 advisory** (all pre-existing `file-placement`).

## Related, not in this PR

This fix stops the silent recurrence; it does not baseline the repos that fell behind. Those were converged by hand this session — thirteen PRs, three already merged. Two gaps this surfaced are worth their own tracking:

1. **Canon PR #555 shipped no migration record.** Making the pack manifest a closed vocabulary with a required `ruleRoutingGuidance` blocks every consumer whose local pack still declares bare `rules` — and because `normalizeManifest` rebuilds `rules` from the scoped lists, such a pack's checks silently stop running. Eleven local packs across ten repos needed hand migration.
2. **No stamp-staleness alarm** (#331). Nothing noticed twelve repos frozen for two days.

All thirteen repos are baselined. Here's what happened.

## The root cause

`deliver()` in the baselining worker never checked the PR-open POST's status:

```js
({ json: pr } = await gh(token, `/repos/${repo}/pulls`, { method: 'POST', ... }));
```

On failure the error body lands in `pr`, auto-merge is skipped silently (no `node_id`), and the run reports `ok`. It compounds because `openMaintenancePull` reuses by *open PR*, not by branch — so each cycle mints a fresh branch. **27 orphan maintenance branches** had piled up across the fleet with no PR behind any of them, while every consumer but the GCEC pilot sat frozen on canon ref `7e89c0cf` from 07-28. GCEC — the one repo with the Actions PR permission enabled — opened and merged its PRs normally throughout.

Fixed in **[Claudinite#584](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/584)** (1015 tests pass, 0 blocking).

## A second, undocumented breakage

Canon PR #555 made the pack manifest a closed vocabulary with a required `ruleRoutingGuidance` — and **shipped no migration record**. Because `normalizeManifest` rebuilds `rules` from the scoped lists, a manifest still declaring bare `rules` doesn't just fail a check: **its rules silently stop running**. That included LaughCounter's never-leaves-the-machine privacy rules and VascularColoring's calibration rules. Eleven local packs across ten repos needed hand migration (`rules` → `worldRules`/`workRules` by each module's declared scope, routing guidance drafted from each pack's own header, bundled skills declared, retired fields dropped).

## Delivered

**Merged** (diff confined to the mount, Actions, and Claudinite settings, as you specified):

| Repo | PR |
|---|---|
| Sheepdog | [#41](https://github.com/missingbulb/Sheepdog/pull/41) |
| MissingBulbWebsite | [#14](https://github.com/missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/pull/14) |
| GoogleCalendarEventCreator | [#804](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/pull/804) |

**Open for review** — each also touches `.claudinite/local/packs/**`, so outside your auto-merge rule: [EdFringeNow#175](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/175) · [TLDR#153](https://github.com/missingbulb/TLDR/pull/153) · [CrosswordChat#105](https://github.com/missingbulb/CrosswordChat/pull/105) · [LaughCounter#89](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/pull/89) · [HelloWorldFlutterApp#72](https://github.com/missingbulb/HelloWorldFlutterApp/pull/72) · [EdFringeAllocator#50](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeAllocator/pull/50) · [ShoutsAndWhispers#56](https://github.com/missingbulb/ShoutsAndWhispers/pull/56) · [gRatio#57](https://github.com/missingbulb/gRatio/pull/57) · [VascularColoring#55](https://github.com/missingbulb/VascularColoring/pull/55) · [ClaudiniteWebsite#32](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/pull/32)

Every repo went to **0 new blocking findings**; all migration notes were already applied and no agentic note was pending. Three repos' pack tests read `pack.rules` and broke — caught by CI on EdFringeNow, fixed and now green.

I counted the generated README badge row as Claudinite wiring for the auto-merge rule, since the diff is confined to its own `<!-- claudinite:packs -->` markers. Say the word if you'd rather that force a review.

> ⚠️ **Needs you — the fix above stops the silence, not the cause:**
> 1. **Enable "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests"** on the twelve consumers. Until then #584 turns a silent stall into a *loud* nightly failure, but baselining still won't land.

input.title: baselining swallows the PR-open failure — branches pile up nightly, stamps freeze, run reports ok
input.body:
## The defect

`deliver()` in `packs/basics/tasks/baselining/worker.mjs` destructured only `json` from the PR-open POST and never read `status`:

```js
({ json: pr } = await gh(token, `/repos/${repo}/pulls`, { method: 'POST', ... }));
```

When that POST fails, the error body lands in `pr`. `pr.node_id` is undefined so the auto-merge arm is skipped silently, the CI dispatch has no PR to attach to, and the run still logs `preprocessing basics/baselining: ok`.

## Why it compounds

`openMaintenancePull` reuses by **open PR**, not by branch. A cycle that pushes its branch but fails to open the PR therefore finds nothing to reuse next cycle and mints a *fresh* branch — nightly — while the stamp never advances and nothing surfaces the failure.

## Observed fleet state (2026-07-29/30)

Eleven of twelve consumers were frozen on canon ref `7e89c0cf` (2026-07-28), each carrying `claudinite/maintenance-2026-07-29-*` and `-07-30-*` branches with **no PR behind either** — several carried two branches for a single day. **27 orphan maintenance branches** in total. GoogleCalendarEventCreator, the pilot and the one repo with the Actions PR permission enabled, opened and merged its maintenance PRs normally throughout.

The usual cause is repo-level and invisible from inside the Action: *Settings → Actions → General → "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests"* is off, so the POST 403s.

## Fix

PR #584 — `pullCreateError(status, json)` as a pure predicate, `null` only on a 201 carrying a PR number; `deliver()` throws on it and the message names the repo setting. See-it-fail coverage for the 403, a 201 with no PR number, and the no-message fallback.

This stops the silence. It does not enable the setting — that stays an owner action on each consumer, and until it is done #584 converts a silent stall into a loud nightly failure.

## Related gaps this surfaced

- **#555 shipped no migration record.** Making the pack manifest a closed vocabulary with a required `ruleRoutingGuidance` blocks every consumer whose local pack still declares bare `rules` — and since `normalizeManifest` rebuilds `rules` from the scoped lists, such a pack's checks **silently stop running**. Eleven local packs across ten repos were migrated by hand this session.
- **No stamp-staleness alarm (#331)** — nothing noticed twelve repos frozen for two days.
- **Seven consumers have no `pull_request` CI at all**, and TLDR's is path-filtered away from `.claudinite/**`, so their maintenance PRs are never gated by the world sweep.

---

content.content:
---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---


The portable recipe for landing the change in front of the owner on `main` — the *mechanics* behind the owner's merge-to-main command (the owner's preferences own the trigger *phrase*; this file owns the *how*). Invoked through the `merge-to-main` skill (this skill); this doc stays the canonical recipe.

**A project's bespoke merge policy overrides this default.** Most projects need nothing here — this default is the whole story. A project that genuinely diverges (a different merge method, a CI/twice-green gate, an extra approval) **states so by naming its merge-policy file explicitly in its own `CLAUDE.md`**. When that declaration is present, read that file first and let it override the divergent points below; when it's absent, follow this default as-is. Don't go hunting for a policy file that the project's `CLAUDE.md` doesn't name.

## Recipe (~4 calls)

1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.
3. Gate on CI **only if the repo has it** — a workflow that actually runs on PRs/pushes. `workflow_call`-only reusable workflows (this repo hosts some) are *not* CI: they never run here, so a non-empty `.github/workflows/` alone proves nothing; check the PR for check runs instead. No CI → no gate; don't wait for checks that will never come.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.

The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.

## After the merge: capture the conversation (every session, every user)

Once the merge has landed and local `main` is synced, run the growth pack's capture step:
`node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>` (from the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), `<n>` being the issue your `Closes #<issue>` named. Deterministic, seconds-long; it pushes the conversation to the orphan `conversation-logs` branch. It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later in the repo's scheduled `conversation-extract` task (MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) owns the standard).
